source.version: EdArXiv preprint, version 2 (DOI 10.35542/osf.io/5a3mn_v2, posted 2025-08-04 per the retrieval record). The document itself carries a note that the manuscript is 'currently under review at a peer-reviewed journal' (p. 1). The journal version of record (Journal of Computer Assisted Learning, 10.1002/jcal.70223, 2026) is not on file.
source.title_on_document: Group-AI collaboration enhances creativity performance: The roles of perspective-taking and AI utilization strategies

supplement.where: The text refers to 'Supplementary Figure 2A' and 'Supplementary Figure 2B' (pp. 12 and 15), but these panels appear as Figure 2A and 2B in the main PDF (p. 13). No separate supplement or online appendix is named.
supplement.holds: Nothing beyond the main text appears to be referenced. All creativity statistics (arm means, SDs, mixed-model coefficients and SEs) are in the main text, pp. 15-16, and Figures 3 and 5.

paper_design_summary: Ninety-six Chinese university students (after excluding 4 of 100 recruited) were randomly paired into two-person teams in a lab and each completed three 15-minute scientific divergent application tasks (novel uses for a new material) under three within-subject conditions: pairs with one ChatGPT-4o each (group-AI), each person alone with ChatGPT-4o (individual-AI), and pairs without AI (human-only group), with condition order presented randomly/counterbalanced. Ideas were scored for usefulness and originality by two LLM raters (ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek), and fluency and high-quality idea fluency were counted; outcomes were compared with mixed-effects models with a subject random effect.

studies.label: Lab experiment: group-AI vs individual-AI vs human-only group on a scientific divergent application task

assignment.what_was_assigned: Participants were randomly paired into two-person teams; each team completed all three collaboration conditions (group-AI, individual-AI, human-only group), with condition order and task material counterbalanced / randomly presented.
assignment.quote: They were then randomly paired to form two-person teams. ... Subsequently, each team was randomly assigned to one of the three collaborative innovation conditions ... The order of conditions and the assignment of tasks were counterbalanced across participants
assignment.locator: pp. 7-8, Section 2.2 Procedure; p. 9, Figure 1B ('Random Presentation' of the three collaborative innovation modes); p. 7, Section 2.1 ('within-subjects experimental design')

arms.name: Group-AI (G-AI)
arms.description: Two-person team takes turns posting one idea per turn in a shared QQ chat; each member has their own ChatGPT-4o and may ask it one question per own turn.

arms.name: Individual-AI (I-AI)
arms.description: Each participant works one-on-one with ChatGPT-4o; the idea panel is private so the partner's inputs are not visible.

arms.name: Human-only group (G)
arms.description: Two-person team takes turns posting ideas in a shared chat; AI interface disabled.

participants.exclusions: 100 participants recruited via an online questionnaire; 4 excluded for failing to follow task instructions, leaving 96 (48 two-person teams implied by F(1, 47) on p. 17; the number of teams is not stated directly). Per-arm n is not printed; it equals 96 only because every participant completed all three conditions. The paper does not say at what stage the 4 were excluded.
participants.who: University students; 64 women; mean age 21.91 (SD 3.51); paid 60 RMB.
participants.quote: A total of 100 participants were recruited via an online questionnaire. Four participants were excluded for failing to follow task instructions, resulting in a final sample of 96 (64 women; Mage = 21.91, SD = 3.51).
participants.locator: p. 7, Section 2.1 Participants; p. 1, Abstract ('96 university students'); pp. 26-27, Discussion ('participants in this study were recruited from China')

ai_tool.how_used: Participants typed prompts to ChatGPT-4o in a panel beside the idea chat. In the group-AI condition each member had their own AI and could ask one task-related question during their own turn; in the individual-AI condition participants collaborated one-on-one with the AI. Participants could copy AI ideas verbatim or adapt them.

task.description: Scientific divergent application task (SDAT, adapted from Wan et al. 2025): generate novel applications for a novel material. Three items used: transparent ceramics, electronic skin, crystal resin; ideas typed one per turn in a QQ chat window.
task.duration: 15 minutes per condition, after a 5-minute pre-test questionnaire (Figure 1B, p. 9)

outcomes.name: Creative usefulness
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Extent ideas could be realistically applied, 5-point scale (1 = not at all useful, 5 = very useful), rated by two LLMs (ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek); ICC between the two models 0.74. Mixed-effects model with Subject ID random effect and condition fixed effect. Mediation models (PROCESS Model 4) also report total and direct effects (Figures 5-6).

eligibility.reason: Within-subject lab experiment: every participant worked with and without generative AI (ChatGPT-4o), with condition order randomly presented / counterbalanced (p. 8; Figure 1B, p. 9); 96 people analyzed (p. 7); usefulness, originality, fluency, and high-quality idea fluency are scored on the ideas by two LLM raters and by counts (p. 10). Caveats: the text describes order as 'counterbalanced' while Figure 1B says 'Random Presentation', and the text also says each team was 'randomly assigned to one of the three' conditions, which conflicts with the within-subject design. People worked in randomly formed pairs in two of the three conditions.

one_line_finding: Pairs in which each member had ChatGPT-4o produced ideas rated more useful (4.09 vs 3.24 human-only pairs, beta = 0.84, SE = 0.04; vs 3.34 individual-AI, beta = 0.74, SE = 0.06) and more original (3.68 vs 2.74 and 2.70) than human-only pairs or individuals with AI, with no fluency difference and no difference between individual-AI and human-only pairs (pp. 15-16, Section 3.1, Figure 3).
open_questions: Unit of the creativity scores in the pair conditions is not stated: are usefulness/originality per participant (mean over own ideas) or per team? The mixed model uses a Subject ID random effect (p. 15), suggesting participant-level scores.

The process comparisons of G-AI vs I-AI use independent-samples t-tests with df = 142 (pp. 18-19, 22), implying about 144 observations, which does not match 96 participants each observed in both conditions; the human-perspective-taking ANOVA uses F(1, 47), implying 48 teams. The number of observations behind the creativity mixed models is not printed.

Procedure text says each team was 'randomly assigned to one of the three collaborative innovation conditions' (p. 7) yet also that 'Each participant completed three experimental conditions' (p. 8); the design is coded as within-subject with randomized/counterbalanced order.

Mediation total effects in Figure 5 (e.g., 0.85 for G-AI vs G usefulness) differ slightly from the mixed-model betas in Section 3.1 (0.84); the Figure 5 models likely include the stated control variables, but the paper does not say.
Whether the stated control variables (ideational behavior, group preference, algorithm aversion, AI trust; p. 10) enter the Section 3.1 mixed models is not stated.
notes: Version on file is the EdArXiv preprint; the 2026 JCAL article (Zhou, Xiao, Wang, Tong, Zhang, Hao) could not be checked. The PDF shows no author names (blind-review note on p. 1). Creativity raters are LLMs (ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek), not humans, so outcomes are coded automated_score. ai_available_when_produced is 'mixed' because AI was available in G-AI and I-AI but not in the human-only group arm; within each AI arm AI was available while ideas were produced. Process outcomes not listed (not creativity scored on the output): human and AI perspective-taking counts and rates, frequency of AI use, prompt-strategy counts, and response time (pp. 17-22). Primary record candidate: G-AI vs human-only group (ai_vs_bau) on usefulness or originality; no overall-creativity rating exists. G-AI vs I-AI is coded ai_design (same AI, solo vs paired configuration); I-AI vs G is coded ai_vs_active (AI partner vs human partner).
